Aerial Wildlife Survey Report  
Wildlife Management Unit 164 Aerial Ungulate Survey (2020) 
 
Background 
Kirkpatrick Wildlife Management Unit 164 (WMU 164), covers an area of 4,261.9 km 2  east and north of Hanna, 
Alberta. The WMU has headwaters and drainages of Berry Creek, Loyalist Creek, Monitor Creek, and Sounding 
Creek. The WMU is entirely within the Grassland Natural Region of Alberta, and contains relatively equal areas of 
dry mixed-grass (south portion of WMU), and northern fescue subregions. The WMU contains large expanses of 
native grassland and agriculture, and is primarily deeded land. There are relatively lar ge tracts of stunted aspen 
forest and willow in the Sounding Creek drainage. 
 
A survey for mule deer was last conducted for WMU 164 in 2009 using the random stratified block methodology 
(Random Block). See Table 1 for previous ungulate survey estimates for  WMU 164. 
 
The objective of the January 2020 survey was to assess the status of deer and moose populations in WMU 164 by 
determining estimates for abundance, density and age-sex composition. We also recorded observations of 
additional species of game management or conservation concern including elk, pronghorn, carnivores, game birds,  
and sensitive or At Risk species.  
Survey method 
The transect survey was conducted flying 47 north-south lines at 1.6 km intervals, with 50% coverage (800 m wide 
survey strip) from Jan 6-10, 2020 for a total linear survey effort of 2,595 km. At each observation point, ungulates 
were classified by species, and when possible, sex and age class was recorded.  Antler size for deer was 
classified as ‘small’ (spike or two points on one or both antlers), ‘medium’ (antlers with 3 or more points; antlers 
inside ears) or large (antlers with ≥ 4 points, antlers outside of ears). 
 
Density was  calculated for white-tailed deer, mule deer and moose following Jolly 1969 (as described in Krebs 
2014) for surveys conducted with unequal sized units without replacement because the transect lengths varied. 
Density was multiplied by the WMU area to determine population estimates. 90% confidence in tervals were also 
calculated. 
 
Elk observations were recorded during the survey, but population estimates were not calculated because the 
design of the survey is not appropriate for elk population  
Results 
A total of 468 white-tailed deer were observed in 88 groups. The estimated density was 0.23 deer/km2  (90% CI 
0.18 – 0.28) and the estimated abundance was 961 individuals (90% CI 747 – 1,174). A total of 451 white-tailed 
deer were successfully classified and the buck:doe:fawn ratio was estimated to be 23:100:42. That results in an 
estimated 2020 early winter white-tailed deer population of 134 buck, 582 doe, and 245 fawn. Of the 63 white-
tailed deer bucks classified, 32 (51%) were classified ‘small’, 27 (43%) ‘medium’, and four (6%) ‘large’. 
 
A total of 1,039 mule deer were observed in 147 groups. The estimated density was 0.50 mule deer/km2  (90% CI 
0.43 – 0.57) and the estimated abundance was 2,133 individuals (90% CI 1,822 – 2,443). A total of 995 mule deer 
were successfully classified and the buck:doe:fawn ratio was estimated to be 55:100:45. That results in an 
estimated 2020 early winter mule deer population of 617 buck, 1,123 doe, and 505 fawn. Of the 275 mule deer 
bucks classified, 109 (40%) were classified ‘small’, 97 (35%) ‘medium’, and 69 (25%) ‘large’.

A total of 123 moose were observed in 66 groups. The estimated density was 0.06 moose/km2  (90% CI 0.05 – 
0.07) and the estimated abundance was 252 individuals (90% CI 196 – 309). A total of 112 moose were 
successfully classified and the bull:cow:calf ratio was estimated to be 90:100:83. That results in an estimated 2020 
early winter moose population of 83 bull, 92 cow, and 77 calf. 
 
A total of 30 elk (16 bull, 9 cow, 5 calf)  and five pronghorn were observed during the survey. 
 
We also observed 179 coyotes, 738 sharp-tailed grouse , five snowy owls, and one red fox .These are incidental 
observations only and should not be considered minimum total counts.
